newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Omni Industries targets 15-20 pct annual growth.
newsitem.headline: Omni Industries targets 15-20 pct annual growth.

text.p: Electronics company Omni Industries Pte Ltd, which is seeking a listing on the Stock Exchange of Singapore, is targetting profit growth of 15 to 20 percent over the next few years, managing director Lee Kim Bock said on Wednesday.
"We are targeting a 15-20 percent per annum growth in turnover and profits in the longer term," Lee said.
Its expansion into manufacturing of plastic car parts, telecommunications equipment and medical instrumentation devices was expected to spur this growth, Lee said.
The bulk of the company's revenue is now generated by contract manufacturing and plastic mould business, each contributing about 45 percent of total sales, he said.
Omni, which is part of the Wuthelam paint conglomerate, is expected to offer 40-50 million shares in its initial public offer shortly.
Group net earnings rose to Singapore $6 million in 1995 from a loss of S$4 million in 1991 while turnover grew to S$140 million from S$15 million during the same period.
Omni will use the money raised from its IPO to expand operations in China, to buy new equipment and to repay bank borrowings.
The company has 10 manufacturing plants in Singapore, Malaysia and China. ($1 = S$1.41) -- Singapore newsroom (65 8703083)
